note: From the OpenStreetMap export (11 October 2026), at real scale across the line like the tracks: two side platforms on the Hazel Grove line, 1.68 m outside its two tracks (trains stop 20 m south of the station's point, in the middle of the platforms, so a six-car unit stands on them extended), Bramhall Lane over the line at the north end (drawn as a landmark, `bramhall-lane`, from the LIDAR; OSM has its bridge from u 61 to 76, crossing at an angle), and the booking office beside the bridge on the east side. Positive v is east. The cutting walls are low because the ground here isn't cut away. Photos (geograph 6133253, 6133297 and 6133304 Gerald England 2019, 3312320 and 3312317 2013, 3831392 and 3831403 2014, 2571096 and 2571093 David Dixon 2011, 1446591 and 1446617 2009, 638662 John Attfield 2007, 3335317 Peter Barr 2013, 826662 and 826668 Peter Whatley): the booking office is an 1880s dark-brick building in the bridge's south-east corner, one storey to the street and two to the platform, under a hipped slate roof (drawn flat). There is no footbridge: passengers cross on Bramhall Lane, down a straight steel stair beside the booking office to the east platform and concrete steps to the west one, both along the line from the bridge (the way across). The west platform has a flat canopy about 30 m long on a white-painted brick building (with the canopy); the east one a small white shelter by the stair, so the canopy is the west platform's only. No lifts in the photos: they're the game's. A small car park shows from a train (geograph 4265476, 2014); OpenStreetMap's API (13 October 2026, way 136355223) puts it on the west side north of Bramhall Lane, a strip beside the line at u 184 to 306, v -29 to -8. Not drawn while the station sells no car park. Departure boards on each platform and by the steps to the booking office; Sheffield stands on the platform with the way across (from memory). Its booking office's roof is hipped (the `hipped` part, 12 October 2026, from the photos in this note; the pitch from memory). Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).
